{"body":"## Summary
`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.

Fixes #1928.

## Changes
- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via the shared `resolveNamedExternalAgent` helper (`external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)`) before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`.
  - Because that view is partial, it **says so**: the header is `Built-in agents:` (not the `--external` view's `Agents:`), and the footer reports when the repo has `external_agents` enabled but is not showing those plugins. Without this, the user who had just run `entire agent add <plugin>` — which turns the gate on — got a listing under a completeness-implying header that silently excluded the agent they had installed, and an empty state reading `No built-in agents installed.`
  - Reading the setting for that footer is one file read and no plugin exec, so the no-scan guarantee is unchanged (`TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath` still passes untouched). The alternative — having the default path honour the gate and discover — was rejected deliberately: `entire agent list` would then change both cost and content off a setting the user never typed.
- **`--external`** is a **superset**: it lists the built-in agents *and* the external plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — installed `✓` marker, sort order, and test-only filter — so the two views differ only where they must (its header is unscoped, and it is the view whose empty state can honestly say `No agents installed.`). External entries carry an `(external)` suffix, because they are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary, and that distinction is trust-relevant.
  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.
- **`printAgentError` (the "Unknown agent" / "Missing agent name" path) no longer contradicts `agent list`**:
  - It goes through the new `agent.ListAvailable`, so test-only agents (`vogon`) are no longer advertised as available.
  - The trailing hint now follows one rule: **it exists only to cover a listing that is knowably incomplete.** What the caller did about `$PATH` before giving up on the name decides which hint, if any, is honest.
    - A full `$PATH` scan already ran, so the listing is complete → **no hint**. This is `enable --agent`, which runs `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` at `setup.go:892` fourteen lines before the failing `agent.Get`: every plugin is already in the listing, marked `(external)`, so pointing at `entire agent list --external` sent the user to repeat a search whose results were four lines above.
    - A targeted single-name lookup ran → `externalAgentSearchedHint(name)`, which names the one plugin that came up missing. This is `agent add` / `agent remove`.
    - No lookup at all → `externalAgentHint`, now down to exactly one caller: the `--agent` `FlagErrorFunc`, which cobra invokes during flag parsing, before `enable`'s `RunE` and so before its scan.
    - `printMissingAgentError` was reached from both sides of that line, so it splits into `…PreDiscovery` / `…PostDiscovery`. `printAgentError` treats an empty hint as omit, with no stray blank line left behind.
  - The usage line follows the caller's command surface (`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` / `entire enable --agent`) instead of always printing `entire enable --agent`.
- **New `agent.ListAvailable() []ResolvedAgent`** is the single place the test-only filter lives; `StringList`, `runAgentList`, `printAgentError`, and `hookAgentOptions` (the interactive agent picker, which carried its own inline `TestOnly` check) all go through it, so "which agents are available" has one answer across the command surface. No inline test-only checks remain outside `registry.go`. It returns name+agent pairs because an external plugin's self-reported `Name()` is not validated against the registry key derived from its binary, and the registry key is the identity users type and `agent.Get` accepts.
  - `agent.Get`'s unknown-agent error was the last unfiltered user-facing listing — `main.go` prints it verbatim where a command doesn't intercept it, and it named `vogon`. It now lists `StringList()`, with the read lock released before the message is formatted so `StringList` (which resolves each agent through `Get`) can't re-enter `registryMu`. That also removes the latent nested `RLock` the old `List()` call had on that line.
  - The pre-existing `List` and `StringList` keep their names. `List` stays deliberately unfiltered because the registry's own plumbing needs every registered name: `hooks_cmd.go` builds the `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands from it and the Vogon binary invokes `entire hooks vogon <verb>`, so filtering there would break every canary test; `external/discovery.go` needs the full set to avoid re-registering a name already taken. Renaming these for clarity is a separate concern and stays out of this PR.
- **New `agent.IsRegistered`** for existence probes. `external/discovery.go` was asking "is this name taken?" by discarding a `Get` error, which built the whole `available: ...` listing (resolving every registered agent) just to answer yes/no.
- `agent.SnapshotForTesting` moved to `cmd/entire/cli/agent/testing.go` — it cannot live in a `_test.go` because package `cli`'s tests need it, and the filename follows `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/testing.go`, the existing precedent for a dedicated cross-package test-helper file. Its doc comment is narrowed: capture/restore are safe against concurrent registry *readers*, not writers, since restore replaces the whole map.
- Docs: `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md` claimed discovery "runs once during CLI initialization". There is no such step — every call site is inside a command, in one of three shapes (gated full scan, ungated full scan, ungated single-name lookup). The Discovery section now documents which commands use which, that `external_agents` gates the first, and how `agent list` and `--external` differ. `CLAUDE.md`'s command-layout entry for `agent` gained the same `list` / `list --external` / `add`-`remove` distinction.
- Drive-by, unrelated to external agents: `agent/architecture_test.go` had `//nolint:staticcheck` separated from the `parser.ParseDir` call by another comment line, where the directive does not apply. Moved onto the offending line.

## Test
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagListsAvailablePlugin`: the default listing does not surface an available external plugin; `--external` lists it.
- `TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath`: asserts on an exec log the mock plugin appends to, proving the default path never execs a plugin while `--external` does — the guarantee the filter-driven absence check above cannot make.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagMarksInstalled`: `--external` lists an installed external plugin marked `✓`.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalIsSuperset`: `--external` includes both the external plugin and the built-ins.
- `TestRunAgentList_MarksExternalProvenance`: external lines carry `(external)`, built-in lines do not.
- `TestRunAgentList_HeaderScopedToMode`: the default header scopes itself to built-ins; `--external`, the complete view, does not.
- `TestRunAgentList_DefaultFooterNamesEnabledGate`: with `external_agents` on, the default listing reports the plugins it is omitting; with the gate unset it prints the plain `--external` pointer and does not claim the gate is on.
- `TestRunAgentList_EmptyStateWording`: mode-scoped empty state — "No built-in agents installed" by default, "No agents installed" under `--external`.
- `TestEnableCmd_UnknownAgent_ListsPluginsAndOmitsHint` executes the real `enable` `RunE` with a mock plugin on `$PATH` and asserts the plugin appears marked `(external)` **and** that no hint follows. This is the test that had to exist: the pre-existing unit test passed only because it called `printWrongAgentError` directly with the hint hardcoded, never triggering the discovery that made the hint wrong. Verified red by reverting just the `enable` call site.
- `TestPrintAgentError_ExcludesTestOnlyAgents`, `TestPrintAgentError_PointsAtExternalListing`, `TestPrintAgentError_HintReflectsWhatWasSearched` (inverted: after a full scan, neither hint wording may appear, and no doubled blank line), `TestAgentAdd_UnknownNameReportsSearchedPath`, and the usage-line assertion in `TestPrintWrongAgentError` cover the error-path fixes.
- `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` covers the registry snapshot helper; `TestIsRegistered` pins that the probe answers for test-only agents too, since it reports registry membership rather than user-facing availability.
- `TestGet_UnknownAgentErrorExcludesTestOnly` pins that `Get`'s error lists real agents and not test-only ones (verified red before green; the package also passes under `-race`, since the fix changes locking).
- The external-plugin tests share one `withExternalAgentPlugin` helper (isolated repo, `#!/bin/sh` mock plugin on a scrubbed `$PATH`, registry snapshot/restore), parameterised on the two axes that actually differ: whether the mock reports its hooks installed, and whether the settings enable `external_agents` — the listing tests opt in, `add`/`remove` deliberately leave it unset because naming a plugin is itself the opt-in. They skip when no POSIX shell is available.

## Verification
- `mise run fmt` — clean
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) — 0 issues
- `mise run test:ci` — PASS
- Benchmark (9 shell plugins on `$PATH`, `external_agents:true`): default `agent list` **18 execs → 0**; external listing moved behind `--external`. Wall clock for the opt-in path, min of 6 runs: default 1.13s vs `--external` 1.69s, i.e. ~60ms per plugin for the two subcommands discovery invokes.

input.summary: Fix + ship agent add/remove path-separator error
input.message:
Code-review finding on PR #1930 (branch fix/1928-agent-group-external-discovery, repo /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/pr-reviews). Please fix it and ship it (commit + push + update the PR), then report back to me.

Finding — cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go:152 (low severity):

`resolveNamedExternalAgent` promotes `discoverAndRegisterNamed`'s validation error into a hard command failure, so a mistyped name containing a path separator bypasses the friendly error path entirely. `entire agent add ./claude-code` (or a completion artifact like `bin/claude-code`) prints the raw:

    loading external agent "./claude-code": invalid external agent name "./claude-code": contains path separators

instead of the `Unknown agent …` message plus the available-agents listing and usage line that every other bad name gets. Same applies to `exec.ErrDot`, which `discoverAndRegisterNamed` also propagates as a non-`ErrNotFound` error when `.` is on `$PATH`.

Suggested fix: treat the path-separator case and `exec.ErrDot` as "no plugin by that name" — fall through to `printWrongAgentError` so the miss path stays uniform across `agent add` and `agent remove`. Keep genuine plugin *load* failures as hard errors (that distinction was deliberate in this PR).

Please add a test covering `entire agent add ./<name>` producing the friendly unknown-agent output. Follow the repo checklist before pushing: `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` (note: use the mise-installed golangci-lint directly if a stale v1 shadows it).

When done, SendMessage back to "cli-d4" with what you changed and the commit/push result.

content.text:

I'll relay its report when it arrives.
